answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-reputation inlet: every new agent must lock a small refundable deposit and earn trust through verified work before it can transact freely, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes costly. Like a lagoon whose narrow inlet limits what flows in, the economy throttles entry while letting honest agents pass. Each agent's history is a distinct pigment in the ledger - copies share the same shade and are easy to spot, so sybils cannot hide among genuine participants.
